summary: Risk-off, and this time it stuck. NQ popped overnight, failed, then trended straight down all session to close 30,138.75, off 2.09 percent and well below a falling stop. MES followed it lower, down 1.15 percent to 7,765, and December gold got sold with everything else, off 1.37 percent to 4,126.9, so there was no safe-haven bid. Crude was the only green, up 0.41 percent to 95.16, but it faded off its high. VIX jumped more than 10 percent to 16.87.

setups.stop: Short while below: MNQ 30,411, MES 7,792, gold 4,144. Long on crude above 94.34.
setups.t1: Session lows on the short side, the 96.07 high on crude.
setups.bias: Clean trend-down day. Indices and gold are below falling stops so the short trend is on, and crude is above a rising stop so its long trend is on, though it faded off the high.

setups.name: AVWAP Bounce
setups.entry: Short a retrace into AVWAP that rejects, with AVWAP now overhead resistance.
setups.stop: Above the AVWAP level that was tested.
setups.bias: Price spent the day below AVWAP. The anchored mean has flipped to resistance, so bounces into it favor the short side.

event.name: No scheduled US release (budget and shutdown disruption continues)
event.consensus: The federal data calendar is still disrupted by the Washington budget and shutdown situation. October CPI and other scheduled releases are delayed and may not print, so there is no reliable data catalyst.
event.actual: No major US release drove the tape. This was a positioning and flow-driven risk-off session.
event.surprise: The selloff itself was the story. A broad, steady de-risking with no single headline, and VIX jumped more than 10 percent off the lows.
event.nqReaction: NQ popped to 30,891.5 overnight, failed, then trended straight down through the US session to a 30,078.5 low, closing 30,138.75 off 2.09 percent, well below a falling stop. A clean trend-down day.
event.crossAsset: MES fell 1.15 percent to 7,765, also below its stop. December gold got sold with the rest, off 1.37 percent to 4,126.9. Crude was the lone green, up 0.41 percent to 95.16 above a rising stop but fading off a 96.07 high. VIX 16.87, up 10.5 percent.

risk.openRisk: Trend-long is off in the indices and gold. The clean trend-long is crude, above a rising stop but fading.
risk.note: The regime is cleanly risk-off. NQ, MES and December gold all sit below falling stops, so systematic trend-long stays off on all three until a two-hourly-close reclaim (MNQ 30,411, MES 7,792, gold 4,144). Today's clean reads were the short side in the indices and gold and the long in crude above 94.34, but crude faded off its high, so trail it and do not add. VIX at 16.87 is up sharply but still not high, so keep size normal and let the stops do the work. An unreliable data calendar and a fast tape argue for discipline over size. Next policy event is the FOMC meeting Oct 27 to 28.

psychology: Yesterday the open dive got bought. Today it did not. No two sessions are the same, so trade what is in front of you, not what worked last time. This was a trend day, where the money is made by staying with the move and lost by fighting it. The failed up-break at 9:45 Eastern was the tell. When a break fails and price closes back under the range, go with the trend or stand aside. Do not pick the bottom.

fullReport.html:
OR High 30,626 | OR Low 30,498 | Width 128 pts (0.42%)

Break UP at 13:45 UTC at 30,647.75, but it failed. Price reversed and closed the session far below the range at 30,175.25, well under NYVWAP 30,296.85. HOF VWAP 30,286.2 never held.

It is Wednesday, so HOF and MID were skipped and BIR and BNC were eligible, but no clean setup formed. The failed up-break rolled straight into a one-way trend down.

A failed up-break that turns into a trend day means the opening pop was a trap. The edge was going with the breakdown, not fading it.
